selected_clusters.name: Source of truth for repository state
selected_clusters.description: Where the authoritative copy of each repository's objects and references lives.

values.label: Repository files on server disks
values.description: Plain Git repositories on the servers' local disks are the authoritative state.

values.label: Write-ahead log in object storage
values.description: An append-only log in object storage is the authority; repositories on disk are derived from it.

values.label: Objects in a distributed hash table
values.description: Git objects are stored individually in a distributed key-value store.

values.label: Blobs plus a relational reference database
values.description: Pack data in blob storage and references in a relational database, two stores to keep consistent.

selected_clusters.name: Replication for durability
selected_clusters.description: How copies of a repository are kept so that a lost machine loses no data.

relations.reading: Choices on Replication for durability require a decision on Source of truth for repository state
relations.rationale: What must be replicated, and where, follows from where the authoritative state lives.

relations.reading: Choices on Replication for durability limit the options on Serving reads
relations.rationale: Serving from the nearest replica needs replicas; a single copy leaves one place to read from.

values.label: Block-level filesystem replication
values.description: The filesystem under Git is replicated block by block between paired machines.

values.label: Three Git replicas with majority writes
values.description: Each repository has three plain Git replicas; a write succeeds once a majority has it.

values.label: Durability delegated to object storage
values.description: The object store holding the log keeps the data durable; servers hold no unique data.

values.label: Single copy on a file server
values.description: One file server holds each repository, reached by RPC, with no replica.

selected_clusters.name: Reference update coordination
selected_clusters.description: How concurrent updates to a repository's references are ordered and made atomic.

relations.reading: Choices on Reference update coordination require a decision on Source of truth for repository state
relations.rationale: Updates are ordered by whatever holds the authoritative references.

values.label: Three-phase commit across replicas
values.description: Reference updates run as a transaction that all replicas vote on.

values.label: Compare-and-swap on the log
values.description: Writers append to the log with a compare-and-swap, without a consensus protocol.

values.label: One server serializes the updates
values.description: The single file server holding the repository applies updates one at a time.

selected_clusters.name: Client data transfer
selected_clusters.description: What a developer's machine downloads to work on a repository.

relations.reading: Choices on Client data transfer limit the options on Serving reads
relations.rationale: On-demand object downloads put every file open on the network, which cache servers near the clients absorb.

values.label: Full clone over the Git protocol
values.description: The client fetches the whole history with standard Git.

values.label: Partial clone with sparse checkout
values.description: The client fetches only the history and files it needs, with standard Git features.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem with on-demand objects
values.description: A virtual filesystem shows every file and downloads objects only when a file is opened.

selected_clusters.name: Serving reads
selected_clusters.description: Where read traffic (fetches, clones, CI checkouts) is served from.

values.label: Nearest up-to-date replica
values.description: Reads go to the closest replica that has the latest state.

values.label: Cache servers near the clients
values.description: Cache servers in each office or region serve objects and forward misses to the origin.

values.label: Stateless servers with a local disk cache
values.description: Any server can serve any repository, rebuilding a warm copy on its local disk from the log.
